question: Indicate which of the following deficits leads to a glycogenosis:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Glucose 6-phosphatase -> inability to convert glucose-6-phosphate to glucose -> accumulation of glucose-6-phosphate -> glycogenosis -> 95% CHAIN: Fructose 1,6-bisphosphatase -> inability to convert fructose 1,6-bisphosphate to fructose 6-phosphate -> disruption in gluconeogenesis -> accumulation of substrates -> glycogenosis -> 95%
enhanced_information: Deficit in Glucose 6-phosphatase leads to glycogenosis by causing the accumulation of glucose-6-phosphate. This is supported by the chain of events where the inability to convert glucose-6-phosphate to glucose results in glycogenosis. The evidence paths linking Glucose-6-Phosphate to Glycogen Storage Disease further support this association.
analysis: Deficit in Glucose 6-phosphatase leads to glycogenosis by causing the accumulation of glucose-6-phosphate, which disrupts normal glycogen metabolism. This is a well-established concept in the field of glycogen storage diseases.
